column1: # WHAT WROTE THIS LINE (docs/design/UNITS-AND-TREES.1.md P6). `aontu
# trace` answers every piece a rule stamped under the component tree:
# the FILE it reached, the document address, the model NODE the
# dispatch matched, and the RULE set that wrote it.
# `unit` and `piece` were the renderer's keys. A file is what `unit`
# always was; `piece` has no successor, the tree being the pieces.
# A rule set read through a name is addressed by it; a table written
# inline at the call has no address of its own and is `#<index>`.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# Every expectation was taken from the canonical port and is held to
# the Go port by this file.
trace-one-rule-one-line
column3: svc: { a: { n:"a" } } out: file("x.ts", emit($.svc, { match: n: string body: ["line " + .n] }))

column1: trace-names-the-rule-set
column3: %r = emit(_, { match: n: string body: ["line " + .n] }) svc: { a: { n:"a" } } out: file("x.ts", emit($.svc, %r))

column1: trace-one-entry-per-line
column3: svc: { a: { n:"a" } } out: file("x.ts", emit($.svc, { match: n: string body: ["one" "two"] }))

column1: trace-two-files
column3: svc: { a: { n:"a" } b: { n:"b" } } out: emit($.svc, { match: n: string body: [file(.n + ".ts", ["x"])] })

column1: trace-no-rule-no-entry
trace-innermost-file-wins
column3: svc: { a: { n:"a" } } out: file("outer.ts", [fragment("h.ts", emit($.svc, { match: n: string body: ["x"] }))])

column1: # A HAND-WRITTEN MAP THAT LOOKS LIKE A FILE is not one: the props of a
# real `file(...)` are always a map, so a node whose `props` is a
# string names no file and holds no piece.
trace-file-shaped-map-is-not-a-file
column3: svc: { a: { n:"a" } } out: [{cmp:"File" props:"x" children:[]} file("y.ts", emit($.svc, { match: n: string body: ["L"] }))]
